html:
SMTO-EML-0021 — Your saved email sender has a setting SMTO can't use

GUID: b35614b1-45b6-5e4f-9a7e-dc5e1ed09cf1
Slug: email-sender-profile-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • One detail saved for this email sender, such as the server name, port or From address, isn't in a form SMTO accepts. Nothing was sent, and your password was never tried.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and find the name of the rejected detail, such as server, from_email, reply_to, auth.username or profile. Knowing which detail failed tells you exactly what to change; "profile" means the overall layout, such as a missing, extra or misspelled item.
  2. Open More options › Parameter Store, select the sender, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. That's where the sender's server, port, addresses and sign-in details are stored.
  3. If the rejected detail is profile, pick the matching Email / SMTP template in the new parameter template list and compare its layout with your saved sender. An extra, missing or misspelled item makes the whole saved sender unusable, and the template shows the expected layout.
  4. Fix that detail: the server must be a plain name like smtp.example.com, the port a whole number, and each address a single email address. Then select Save. SMTO checks these exact rules before it will connect to a mail server.

What success looks like

  • After you ask SMTO in a conversation to test the connection for this sender, the test returns a result from the mail server instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change your email password because of this error; SMTO stopped before trying it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Email / SMTP profile validation (validate_profile) rejected a saved sender field before any connection was opened; no authentication rejection is established.

What this means

  • A saved sender field does not meet the Email / SMTP profile contract. No authentication rejection is established. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • A sender configuration field fails its typed contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Check the field named in the error facts (profile, server, from_email, reply_to, envelope_from, from_name, display_name or auth.username) against PROFILE_SCHEMA and validate_profile in src/gateway_core/email_contract.py: profile_type email_smtp, profile_version 1, integer port 1–65535, hostname or IP server, single valid addresses, no control characters. Correct the Parameter Store record, then run email.test_connection before diagnosing credentials.
  • Correct the indicated saved profile field. Test the corrected connection before diagnosing credentials.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The saved profile validates and the connection test reports its actual outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
